title: Longitudinal Clinical and MRI Changes Suggestive of Subclinical Disease Progression in Egyptian Patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Background Progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to disability accumulation in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), reflecting ongoing neurodegeneration despite apparent control of inflammatory disease activity. However, longitudinal data integrating comprehensive clinical assessment with quantitative MRI biomarkers remain limited, particularly in North African populations. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 50 patients with RRMS. Assessments at baseline, 6, and 12 months included the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT), Nine-Hole Peg Test (9-HPT), Timed 25-Foot Walk Test (T25-FWT), and Arabic Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (A-MFIS). Quantitative brain MRI, including regional volumetric analysis, cortical thickness measurements, and white matter lesion assessment, was performed at baseline and after one year. Results During the one-year follow-up, significant deterioration was observed in disability, cognitive performance, upper-limb function, and fatigue, whereas walking performance remained relatively stable. Clinically meaningful cognitive decline (≥ 4-point reduction in SDMT score) occurred in 24% of patients after 6 months and in 44% after one year. EDSS worsening was observed in eight patients at 6 months and seven patients at one year, including progression in 10.3% of patients without documented relapse during the second follow-up period. Quantitative MRI demonstrated significant longitudinal changes in multiple cortical and subcortical brain regions despite stable white matter lesion burden, and clinical deterioration was associated with regional brain volumetric alterations involving the thalamus, cortical and total gray matter, cerebellum, and temporal structures. Older age, longer disease duration, greater relapse burden, and delayed initiation of disease-modifying therapy (DMT) were associated with less favorable clinical outcomes and greater brain atrophy, whereas higher educational attainment and monosymptomatic disease onset were associated with better longitudinal cognitive performance. Conclusion One-year longitudinal follow-up demonstrated measurable changes across multiple clinical domains and regional brain structures consistent with early subclinical disease progression in RRMS despite limited inflammatory activity. Quantitative MRI combined with sensitive cognitive and functional assessments detected changes beyond those captured by conventional disability measures, supporting their complementary role in monitoring early neurodegenerative progression.

title: Single‑port endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy combined with prosthesis breast reconstruction in breast cancer: a retrospective single-center study of 167 cases
abstract: Abstract Background Single‑port endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy combined with prosthetic breast reconstruction (E-NSM-PBR) has been used for breast repair due to aesthetic considerations. However, the clinical feasibility, postoperative complications and oncological safety of E-NSM-PBR in breast surgery remain controversial. This study presents our experience with the application of E-NSM-PBR in breast cancer patients and reports the preliminary results. Methods This is a retrospective study of 167 patients who underwent breast surgery using E-NSM-PBR at our institution between March 1, 2023 and December 31, 2024. Their clinicopathological characteristics, postoperative complications, cosmetic outcomes, and oncologic outcomes were analyzed. Results All patients underwent nipple-sparing mastectomy under single-port endoscopy, followed by breast prosthesis reconstruction. The average duration of unilateral surgery is 222.9 minutes (ranging from 115 to 537 minutes). The average operation time on both sides was 371 minutes (ranging from 348 to 390 minutes). The average reconstruction volume was 253.6 ml (ranging from 100 to 445 ml). The overall complication rate was 16.8%. The subcutaneous fluid and infection in the breast area are the most common complications in breast reconstruction, with a total of 18 cases (10.2%). The combined necrosis rate of the nipple-areola complex (NAC) and skin flaps is 3.6%. There were 3 cases of implant loss after postoperative radiotherapy. The incidence of bleeding complications was the lowest, only 1.2%. Cosmetic outcomes were satisfactory in 94.6% of patients on a four-point scale by three-panel assessment and 95.8% using the BCCT.core software. After a median follow-up of 29 months, one local and one systemic recurrence were observed. Conclusions E-NSM-PBR is a safe and feasible immediate breast reconstruction technique with concealed surgical incision and promising oncologic safety. For suitable candidates, E-NSM-PBR technology can provide good cosmetic results.

title: Lightweight Deep Learning for Processing 3D Medical Images: A Systematic Review
abstract: Abstract Deep learning for three dimension (3D) modalities such as CT, MRI, and PET offers promise to improve diagnostic accuracy, surgical planning, and visualization of disease progression, as 3D image data provide high resolution volumetric representation. However, 3D deep learning models are computationally heavy and demand powerful hardware that is not always available or affordable, restrictingtheir use in resource-constrained settings such as rural clinics, edge devices, and low- and middle-income countries. Hence, there is a growing interest in building lightweight deep learning models, in general, and for 3D imaging, in particular. This article systematically and critically reviews lightweight deep learning for processing 3D medical images, examining model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation, quantization, pruning and efficient architectural designs, together with the datasets, tools, and deployment environments involved. These techniques substantially reduce parameters, memory, and inference time with modest accuracy loss. We also identify several research gaps in these approaches, such as the accuracy mismatch between lightweight and standard models, difficulty handling small anatomical structures while keeping models compact, limited testing on real resource-constrained hardware, weak integration of clinical information, and the absence of efficiency-aware evaluation metrics. We outline future directions, cluding robust lightweight designs, purpose-built compact 3D datasets, standardized efficiency metrics, and lightweight multimodal models.

title: Culler-Jones Syndrome Across Three Generations: Variable Expressivity of a Pathogenic GLI2 Variant—a Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Culler-Jones syndrome is a rare developmental disorder associated with pathogenic variants in GLI2 gene. The phenotype is highly variable and may include hypopituitarism, growth hormone deficiency, postaxial polydactyly, craniofacial abnormalities, and other developmental abnormalities involving midline structures. Variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance can complicate diagnosis and genetic counseling, particularly when relatives carrying the same pathogenic variant have few or no apparent manifestations. Case presentation A 24-year-old woman of Native American ancestry on both the maternal and paternal sides of her family was referred to the Adult Genetics Clinic for evaluation of congenital craniofacial abnormalities, hypopituitarism, growth hormone deficiency, short stature, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Her history included bilateral cleft lip, anterior cleft palate, midline upper lip and gingival tissue masses, severe growth delay, and abnormal pubertal development. Brain magnetic resonance imaging performed in early childhood demonstrated a Chiari I malformation and absence of most or all of the pituitary gland. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in GLI2 , NM_005270.4:c.1421G>A (p.Trp474*). Targeted familial testing subsequently identified the same variant in her mother, sister, and maternal grandmother, all of whom were reportedly without significant manifestations of GLI2 -related disease. Her brother tested negative for the familial variant. The maternal family history was notable for postaxial polydactyly in multiple relatives. Two maternal uncles reportedly had both postaxial polydactyly and multiple supernumerary nipples, with up to five additional nipples reported in affected individuals. These relatives were not available to undergo genetic testing. Conclusions This family demonstrates marked variable expressivity associated with a pathogenic GLI2 variant across three generations. The proband had a severe multisystem phenotype, whereas three relatives carrying the same variant were reportedly without significant manifestations. Multiple supernumerary nipples in two maternal relatives who have not had molecular confirmation of the GLI2 familial variant represent a potentially new phenotype finding that has not been established as part of the recognized phenotype of Culler-Jones syndrome. This case highlights the importance of detailed family history assessment, cascade testing, and careful genetic counseling in families with GLI2 -related disease.

title: Canadian Preterm Brain Injury Consensus Classification for Cranial Ultrasound and Prediction of Neurodevelopmental Outcome in Preterm Infants
abstract: Abstract Objective To determine whether classification of severe preterm brain injury using the Canadian cranial ultrasound (cUS) consensus improves prediction of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Study Design Infants born < 29 weeks’ gestation (2010–2018) with ≥ 3 cUS examinations, any brain injury, and neurodevelopmental assessment at 18–24 months were studied. Brain injury was assessed from serial cUS using the Canadian consensus classification. Severe injury comprised high-grade intraventricular hemorrhage, severe post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation, cystic white matter injury, and/or moderate-large cerebellar hemorrhage. Associations with death and/or significant neurodevelopmental impairment were analyzed and compared with historical reporting. Results Among 231 infants, 45% had severe brain injury and 39% experienced adverse outcome. Severe injury was independently associated with adverse outcome (OR 5.44, 95% CI 2.85–10.74). Sensitivity was similar to historical reporting, but specificity for cerebral palsy and severe cognitive delay was higher. Conclusions The Canadian cUS consensus classification improves neurodevelopmental outcome prediction and may inform early intervention and neuroprotective strategies.

title: Duality of Rarity of Chemotherapy-induced Flagellate Erythema among Cancer Patients: A Case Report with 26 Years of Evidence in Oncology.
abstract: Introduction Flagellate Dermatitis (FD) due to anticancer therapy is a rare, unusual Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) in oncology. The current case describes the impact of financial constraints on the choice of anticancer therapy, the occurrence of FD and poor outcomes among Hodgkin's Lymphoma patients, and 26 years of evidence on FD due to anticancer therapy. Case report A 25-year-old male presented with fever, cough, night sweats, weight loss, and swelling on the right side of the neck, which was diagnosed as Hodgkin's Lymphoma with a complex diagnostic work-up (PET-CT scan, histopathology/immunohistochemistry reports). The patient was planned for Nivolumab-AVD therapy, but treated with ABVD chemotherapy due to financial constraints. Unfortunately, the patient developed linear streaks on the trunk region of the body after 4 days of 1st dose of ABVD therapy, which was diagnosed as FD triggered by Bleomycin. Thus, Bleomycin was omitted from the polychemotherapy regimen (AVD), and ADR was managed with corticosteroids. Although the PET-CT report initially showed a partial response to ABVD/AVD. Later, the disease was found to be metabolically progressive, for which salvage therapy (GDP, DHAP, and palliative radiotherapy) was given. Further, the patient was suggested Brentuximab and Nivolumab therapy, but the patient declined therapy due to financial constraints, lack of funding, and coverage by the government healthcare scheme. Thus, the patient was discharged against medical advice. Conclusion Healthcare professionals should be aware of and vigilant for this whip-like dermatological manifestation (FD) when choosing Bleomycin-based therapy. A patient-centric approach to cessation or rechallenge with the culprit drug, along with antihistamines and topical/ oral corticosteroids, is the mainstay for the management of FD.

title: Surgical treatment of large vestibular schwannomas with hydrocephalus in octogenarians: Two cases with favorable functional outcomes.
abstract: Background The optimal management of vestibular schwannoma (VS) associated with hydrocephalus in octogenarians remains controversial. We report two patients aged 80 years or older with Koos grade IV VS who underwent surgical treatment. Case description Case 1 involved an 86-year-old woman who presented with progressive gait disturbance caused by a 3.5-cm cystic right VS associated with hydrocephalus. Case 2 involved an 81-year-old woman who presented with cognitive impairment and gait disturbance due to a 3.0-cm cystic left VS with hydrocephalus. In both patients, magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated narrowing of the high-convexity sulci, enlarged Sylvian fissures, and an acute callosal angle. Tumor resection was performed via a retrosigmoid approach with intraoperative facial motor evoked potential (FMEP) monitoring. Tumor dissection was terminated when FMEP amplitudes decreased to <50% of baseline values, resulting in subtotal or near-total tumor resection. Neither patient developed clinically significant postoperative facial nerve dysfunction. Both patients regained independent ambulation. Postoperative imaging demonstrated reduction of ventricular enlargement and improvement of hydrocephalus-related radiological findings. Cognitive function improved substantially in Case 2, with the Mini-Mental State Examination score increasing from 11 to 24. At the latest follow-up, the first patient remained independent without tumor progression or recurrent hydrocephalus 5.9 years after surgery, whereas the second patient maintained independent daily functioning without evidence of tumor progression at 8 months postoperatively. Conclusion Surgical resection with intraoperative facial nerve monitoring may provide favorable functional and radiological outcomes in carefully selected octogenarians with large VSs associated with hydrocephalus.

title: Rapid enlargement of a cervicomedullary junction neurenteric cyst with de novo fluid-fluid level formation.
abstract: Background Neurenteric cysts are rare congenital lesions that usually follow an indolent course. In cystic lesions, a fluid-fluid level generally indicates hemorrhage; in neurenteric cysts, it is seldom reported and poorly understood. Prior explanations rested largely on imaging and intraoperative inference. We report a cervicomedullary junction neurenteric cyst that enlarged rapidly after indolent growth, with a de novo fluid-fluid level in the absence of hemorrhage, and propose a histopathologically supported mechanism. Case description A 52-year-old man presented with posterior neck pain and dizziness. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a 22-mm cystic lesion. Imaging 17 years earlier showed a 14-mm lesion. Over the next month, the cyst enlarged to 26 mm, developing a de novo fluid-fluid level and perilesional edema. Although suspected, hemorrhage was not confirmed at surgery or on histopathology; the cyst contained viscous proteinaceous fluid. The resected cyst wall showed foam cell clusters, interpreted as indirect evidence of prior wall disruption. Complete resection was achieved without neurological deterioration or recurrence at 8 months. Conclusion A fluid-fluid level in a neurenteric cyst does not necessarily indicate hemorrhage. It may instead reflect a rise in intracystic pressure from chronic mucin secretion that progressively compromises the cyst wall, allowing osmotic influx of cerebrospinal fluid that drives rapid enlargement and dilutes the upper layer. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report in which foam cell clusters provide histological support for such a non-hemorrhagic mechanism in a neurenteric cyst. Interval growth or perilesional edema may precede deterioration and should prompt consideration of timely intervention.

title: Intraoperative motor-evoked potential monitoring during coil embolization of internal carotid-anterior choroidal artery aneurysms: A comparative case series and lessons on monitoring pitfalls.
abstract: Background Ischemic injury to the anterior choroidal artery (AChA) territory during coil embolization of internal carotid artery-AChA (ICA-AChA) aneurysms can be functionally devastating and is not always detected by angiography. We examined the utility and the interpretive pitfalls of intraoperative motor-evoked potential (MEP) monitoring in this specific aneurysm subgroup. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 16 consecutive patients who underwent coil embolization for ICA-AChA aneurysms at a single institution. Seven patients (2013-2025) were monitored with intraoperative MEP (MEP group); 9 patients (2005-2015) treated before monitoring was introduced served as a historical comparison group (non-MEP group). Angiographic AChA changes, MEP waveform changes, intraoperative interventions, and postoperative diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging were analyzed. Results Significant MEP amplitude reduction (≥50%) occurred in two monitored patients, prompting coil retrieval, microcatheter repositioning, or a procedural pause; amplitudes recovered in all. One patient showed transient MEP reduction without angiographic change (possible false-positive). No patient in the MEP group developed postoperative infarction (0%), whereas two of nine non-MEP patients did (22%). Conclusion In this small comparative series, MEP monitoring provided functional information complementary to angiography, with no infarctions in the monitored group. MEP changes must be interpreted alongside angiographic and clinical findings, as both false-positive and false-negative results occur. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

title: Microsurgical resection of a pure third ventricular craniopharyngioma through an interhemispheric transcallosal transforaminal approach.
abstract: Background Craniopharyngiomas account for approximately 2-4% of all intracranial tumors and demonstrate a bimodal age distribution, typically affecting children aged 5-9 years and adults aged 55-69 years. Third ventricular craniopharyngiomas are rare, benign epithelial tumors that may arise primarily within the third ventricle or secondarily extend from the suprasellar region; the purely intraventricular subtype is particularly rare, with a reported incidence ranging from 0.5% to 14% of all cases. Despite benign histology, infiltration of adjacent neural tissue imparts clinically aggressive behavior and complicates complete resection. Their deep location near the hypothalamus, optic apparatus, and fornices poses major surgical challenges, and transcallosal approaches risk cognitive or memory deficit. A purely third ventricular craniopharyngioma, classified as Type D by Yaşargil and Type IV by Kassam, is confined to the third ventricle and is not accessible through an endonasal approach, making transcranial routes more suitable given the tumor's deep location and proximity to critical neurovascular structures, although select cases of successful endonasal resection have been reported. Case description We present a 34-year-old woman with galactorrhea and progressive weight gain over 6 months, together with intermittent diplopia and headaches. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a homogeneously contrast-enhancing mass occupying the third ventricle, measuring 3.0 × 2.9 × 2.3 cm, with preservation of the pituitary stalk and third ventricular floor, causing moderate obstructive hydrocephalus. An interhemispheric transcallosal transforaminal approach was performed, with the dural opening adjusted according to the drainage pattern of the bridging veins, a 1.5 cm callosotomy, and septal fenestration. Gross total resection was achieved with preservation of the pituitary stalk, and a third ventriculostomy was performed to allow cerebrospinal fluid flow. Postoperative magnetic resonance imaging confirmed complete resection, and histopathological examination confirmed a World Health Organization Grade I papillary craniopharyngioma. Surveillance imaging at 27 months confirmed tumor recurrence, and the patient was referred for radiation therapy, after which no further recurrence was observed. Follow-up imaging at 48 months demonstrated continued absence of disease. Conclusion Although there are reports of purely intraventricular craniopharyngiomas resected through the endonasal route, traditional transcranial approaches remain the standard for tumors located entirely within the third ventricle. Although this case was treated before routine molecular testing and targeted therapy became standard, modern management now requires a multidisciplinary strategy integrating microsurgery, radiotherapy, and targeted therapy with BRAF (B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase) and MEK (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase) inhibitors when appropriate.

title: Challenges in diagnosis and management of traumatic diaphragmatic injuries: experiences from a regional New Zealand trauma centre.
abstract: Background Diaphragmatic injury is a rare but serious consequence of thoraco-abdominal trauma, often overlooked due to its subtle initial presentation. Early recognition and surgical intervention of traumatic diaphragmatic injury (TDI) are paramount to treat life-threatening injuries, yet the diagnosis remains challenging due to the non-specific nature of symptoms and the limitations of conventional imaging techniques. This study aims to examine the burden of TDI among trauma patients of all injury severities presenting to the Level 1 trauma centre in New Zealand and evaluate the utility of pre-operative imaging in detecting patients who require operative repair of TDI. Method A retrospective review of the Te Manawa Taki (TMT) Region's trauma registry from 2014 to 2023, with TDIs identified using Abbreviated Injury Scale diagnosis codes 440602, 440604, 440606, 440608, 440610 and 440699, was conducted. This is complemented by a review of clinical records of TDI patients admitted to the Level 1 trauma centre in the TMT Region to evaluate pre-operative imaging techniques used. Results The diagnosis of TDI was made pre-operatively in 29 of 43 patients (67.4%). The injury was visible on chest X-ray (CXR) in 19 patients (44%) and on computed tomography (CT) alone in 26 patients (81%). In 14 patients (32.5%) the diagnosis was only made intraoperatively. The detection rate of radiological imaging is significantly lower than intraoperative detection (rate ratios for CXR and CT are 0.44 and 0.81, respectively; p<0.05). Conclusion TDI remains a rare and challenging diagnosis to establish solely through radiological imaging. Since TDI is often linked with other injuries, a low threshold for surgical intervention could be considered.

title: Prognostic value of the Epidural Spinal Cord Compression scale, Revised Tokuhashi, and Spine Instability Neoplastic Scores in primary stereotactic body radiotherapy for spinal bone metastases.
abstract: Objective Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has emerged as a highly effective, noninvasive treatment for spinal bone metastases (SBMs). However, long-term outcomes of primary SBRT and the comparative prognostic performance of commonly used decision-making tools remain incompletely defined. This study evaluated long-term local control (LC) and systematically compared the predictive value of the Epidural Spinal Cord Compression (ESCC) grade, Spine Instability Neoplastic Score (SINS), and revised Tokuhashi score (rTS). Methods The authors retrospectively analyzed 330 patients with 537 SBMs treated with primary CyberKnife SBRT between 2012 and 2023. SBMs with surgical indications under the NOMS (neurological, oncological, mechanical, and systemic) framework, defined as high-grade epidural compression (ESCC grade 2 or 3) and/or spinal instability (SINS > 12), were excluded. LC was defined as absence of radiographic tumor regrowth ≥ 6 months post-SBRT. Cox proportional hazards models identified independent predictors of local progression (LP). Prognostic discrimination of the ESCC grade, SINS, rTS, and a novel integrated multivariable model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results The 1- and 2-year LC rates were 86.2% and 75.9%, respectively, with a median time to LP of 12 months. Independent predictors of LP included radioresistant histology, epidural compression, pain, osteolytic destruction, single-fraction equivalent dose < 20 Gy, and repeat SBRT. Even minimal epidural compression was strongly associated with inferior LC (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.01, p < 0.001). SBMs with SINS 7-12 also demonstrated significantly worse LC compared with SINS < 7 (aHR 1.78, p = 0.002). The prognostic contribution of rTS was largely driven by performance status alone. ROC analysis showed that the integrated model consistently outperformed the ESCC grade, SINS, and rTS at 1, 3, and 5 years (area under the curve 0.72-0.75 vs 0.59-0.65, all p < 0.05). Acute adverse events occurred in 33.9% of treated SBMs, predominantly pain flare (14.2%). Vertebral fractures developed in 17.0%, 24.2% of which were associated with LP. Conclusions Primary SBRT for SBMs provided durable LC with acceptable toxicity. Although the ESCC grade, SINS, and rTS offered moderate prognostic utility, an integrated multivariable model incorporating tumor, anatomical, and clinical factors demonstrated superior predictive accuracy. Comprehensive risk stratification may refine patient selection and optimize SBRT strategies.

title: Beyond TMJ pain: resolution of diffuse cervicobrachialgia after excision of a TMJ synovial cyst. An atypical case report.
abstract: Synovial cysts of the temporomandibular joint are rare, typically manifesting with local symptoms such as preauricular pain and swelling; magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosis. A 45-year-old woman presented with left preauricular pain, limited mouth opening (maximum interincisal distance of approximately 24 mm), and chronic diffuse cervicobrachialgia radiating from the neck to the fingertips. MRI revealed a 6.2-mm cystic lesion at the posteromedial aspect of the left TMJ, associated with disc displacement. Surgical excision via a preauricular approach resulted in complete removal of the cyst, which was confirmed by postoperative computed tomography (CT). Cervicobrachialgia resolved within one week postoperatively. The patient also experienced transient facial paresthesia, which completely subsided within one month. These findings, together with the known overlap between TMJ and cervical innervation, suggest that TMJ synovial cyst excision may alleviate both local and referred distant pain. For general dentists, persistent preauricular pain associated with limited mandibular opening and atypical cervicobrachial symptoms should raise suspicion of intra-articular TMJ pathology when routine dental and musculoskeletal evaluations are inconclusive. Early recognition and referral for MRI assessment may facilitate definitive diagnosis and appropriate management.
